helion.configuration.title: Helion Settings
helion.configuration.enabled.tooltip: Routes world rendering through the Helion render core. Turning it off renders the world with vanilla Minecraft.
helion.configuration.debugMode.tooltip: Shows every Helion value on screen, measures GPU time per render stage and writes JSON lines to logs/helion-debug.jsonl every second. The J key runs a parity check. Costs nothing while off.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.to: Soft shadows in corners, under objects and where blocks meet.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.en: Turns ambient occlusion on or off.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.al: GTAO is the classic method. VISIBILITY_BITMASK gives every occluder a thickness so light passes behind thin objects like fences, grass and torches, which avoids dark halos behind them.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.qu: Higher quality uses more samples for smoother shadows and costs more GPU time.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.st: How dark the shadows get. 1.0 is the default.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.ra: How far, in blocks, nearby surfaces cast shadows.
helion.configuration.ambientOcclusion.de: Shows the ambient occlusion alone in grey, for checking and tuning.
helion.configuration.image.tooltip: Bloom around bright lights, tone mapping and exposure of the final picture.
helion.configuration.image.toneMapper.to: NEUTRAL keeps vanilla colors and only rolls off bright highlights. FILMIC adds film-like contrast, richer colors and whiter cores in bright glows. NONE clips bright colors like vanilla.
helion.configuration.image.exposure.tool: Brightens or darkens the picture in camera stops. 0 keeps the vanilla brightness.
Adjusts the brightness like an eye: brighter in caves and dark places, darker when the ground is very bright. Only brightens, by up to half a camera stop; daylight keeps the vanilla brightness.
helion.configuration.image.colorGrade.to: A color look applied after tone mapping, like a film grade: Neutral keeps the colors, Warm and Cool shift the white balance, Vivid adds saturation, Cinematic adds contrast and a warm tint, Muted softens the colors.
helion.configuration.image.edgeSmoothing: A light anti-aliasing filter that softens jagged block edges in one quick pass, like FXAA. Used only while temporal anti-aliasing is off.
helion.configuration.image.dither.toolti: Adds invisible fine noise that removes color banding in the sky and in smooth gradients.
helion.configuration.image.bloom.tooltip: A soft glow around bright light sources such as lava, torches, glowstone and the sun.
helion.configuration.image.bloom.intensi: How strong the glow is. 0.5 is the default.
helion.configuration.image.bloom.thresho: How bright something must be to glow. Higher values make fewer things glow. It rises on its own in daylight so snow and sand do not glow.
helion.configuration.image.bloom.debugVi: Shows the bloom glow alone, for checking and tuning.
helion.configuration.image.sharpening.to: Brings back fine block texture detail that looks soft on high resolution screens.
helion.configuration.image.sharpening.st: How strong the sharpening is. Edges that are already sharp are left alone. 0.5 is the default.
helion.configuration.image.motionBlur.to: Blurs the picture along the direction the camera moves or turns, like a film camera.
helion.configuration.image.motionBlur.en: Turns motion blur on or off. Off by default while it is experimental.
helion.configuration.image.motionBlur.st: How long the blur is, the same at every frame rate: 0.5 is like a film camera at 30 frames per second with a half-open shutter, 1 is the full movement of a thirtieth of a second.
Blurs what is far in front of or behind the point you look at, like a camera lens. Focus follows the center of the screen.
Turns depth of field on or off. Off by default while it is experimental.
How wide the lens is: more strength blurs more and starts closer to the focus.
helion.configuration.geometryBuffer.tool: Foundation for Helion's own lighting: terrain is drawn by Helion's own shaders, which also record surface direction, block light, sky light and base color for every pixel. The picture stays identical to vanilla.
helion.configuration.geometryBuffer.enab: Draws terrain through the geometry buffer. Off by default while it is experimental.
helion.configuration.geometryBuffer.view: Shows one recorded value instead of the picture, for checking: NORMALS (surface direction), BLOCK_LIGHT, SKY_LIGHT ALBEDO (base color) or VOXEL_SLICE (the voxel lighting block map at camera height, seen from above). NONE shows the normal picture.
helion.configuration.lighting.tooltip: Helion lights terrain itself from the geometry buffer in high dynamic range: block light and sky light are computed separately, so light can get brighter than vanilla allows. Needs the geometry buffer.
helion.configuration.lighting.enabled.to: Lights terrain with Helion instead of the vanilla light map. Works only while the geometry buffer is on. Off by default while it is experimental.
helion.configuration.lighting.blockLight: Strength of torches, lanterns, lava and other light blocks. 1.0 uses vanilla light levels without the vanilla brightness cap, so surfaces right next to a light can already be brighter than vanilla. Higher values make lights stronger and let lit surfaces glow with bloom.
helion.configuration.lighting.skyLightIn: Strength of daylight and moonlight. 1.0 matches vanilla. Higher values brighten shade, dusk and night; full daylight keeps its vanilla brightness.
helion.configuration.lighting.lightOnlyV: Shows terrain in white with only Helion's light on it, for checking the lighting.
helion.configuration.dynamicLights.toolt: Torches, lanterns, glowstone, lava buckets and other glowing items light up their surroundings while they are held or lie on the ground, and burning mobs light up the area around them.
helion.configuration.dynamicLights.enabl: Lets glowing items in hands, dropped glowing items and burning mobs light the blocks and mobs around them, without changing the world. Costs almost nothing.
helion.configuration.temporalAntiAliasin: Smooths jagged block edges and shimmering textures by moving the camera by less than a pixel every frame and blending each frame with the previous ones.
Turns temporal anti-aliasing on. The picture gets a little softer; sharpening in the image settings restores crisp textures. Off by default while it is experimental.

Renders the world at a lower resolution and rebuilds the full resolution picture over several frames with temporal anti-aliasing, like FSR or TSR. Native keeps the full resolution. Menus and the hand always stay at full resolution.
helion.configuration.physicalSky.tooltip: Replaces the flat vanilla sky color with a sky computed from how sunlight and moonlight scatter in a real atmosphere: deep blue overhead, bright haze around the sun, warm sunsets and a moonlit night. It draws its own sun, a three-dimensional moon and a realistic night sky.
helion.configuration.physicalSky.enabled: Turns the physical sky on in the Overworld. Off by default while it is experimental.
helion.configuration.physicalSky.starDen: How many stars the night sky shows: LOW like a sky near a town, MEDIUM like the countryside, HIGH like a dark sky far from any light.
helion.configuration.physicalSky.milkyWa: Shows a faint band of the Milky Way across dark, moonless nights.
helion.configuration.physicalSky.lightSh: Rays of sunlight and moonlight that stream through gaps in the clouds, between leaves and past the edges of blocks when you look toward the sun or the moon. They pass through glass and water. Needs the physical sky.
helion.configuration.shadows.tooltip: Lets the sun, and the moon at night, cast real shadows from blocks onto terrain. Shadows move with the sun through the day. Needs the geometry buffer, HDR lighting and the physical sky.
helion.configuration.shadows.enabled.too: Turns shadows on. They cost GPU time because the world is drawn once more from the sun. Off by default while they are experimental.
helion.configuration.shadows.quality.too: Resolution of the shadow maps. Higher quality gives sharper shadow edges and uses more video memory.
helion.configuration.clouds.tooltip: Replaces the flat vanilla clouds with real volumetric clouds that are lit by the physical sky: bright edges toward the sun, orange undersides at sunset and soft shadows inside. They drift with the wind and thicken in rain. Needs the physical sky; with it off, or in other dimensions, the vanilla clouds stay.
helion.configuration.clouds.enabled.tool: Turns the volumetric clouds on. Turning clouds off in the vanilla video settings also turns them off. Off by default while they are experimental.
helion.configuration.clouds.quality.tool: Low draws the clouds at a quarter of the resolution with fewer steps. Medium draws them at a third, High at half the resolution with more detail and a high, thin cirrus layer.
helion.configuration.voxelLighting.toolt: Light from torches, lanterns and other glowing blocks is traced through a block map around the camera, so it takes the color of its source and walls cast shadows. Light beyond 64 blocks and held torches keep the vanilla light.
OFF keeps the vanilla block light and does no work at all. SHADER traces colored, shadowed block light on any Vulkan graphics card. Needs HDR lighting. The Voxel Slice geometry buffer view shows the block map from above.
helion.configuration.voxelLighting.quali: Low traces the strongest light of each pixel at half resolution, Medium the two strongest, High the four strongest at full resolution.
helion.configuration.voxelLighting.bounc: Light from torches, lava and other light blocks bounces off walls, floors and ceilings once and takes their color, so it reaches around corners and fills shaded sides softly. Probes every 4 blocks trace a few rays per frame and keep the result over several frames.
helion.configuration.rayTracing.tooltip: Uses the ray tracing hardware of RTX and similar graphics cards for effects shaders cannot do well. Needs a card with hardware ray tracing; on other cards it stays off.
Builds a ray tracing copy of the blocks within about 64 blocks of you. Needs a graphics card with hardware ray tracing and takes effect after restarting the game.
helion.configuration.rayTracing.waterRef: Water mirrors the blocks, the sky, the sun and the moon above it, with small waves; deep water gets darker so reflections stand out.
Within about 64 blocks of you, sun and moon shadows are traced against the real block shapes: leaves, fences and flowers cast shadows with their holes, and edges get softer the farther they fall from what casts them. Needs sun and moon shadows to be on.
helion.toggle.title: Helion
helion.state.disabled: Render core disabled, vanilla rendering is used
helion.passive.title: Helion is inactive
helion.passive.not_vulkan: Helion needs Vulkan. Set Graphics API to Prefer Vulkan in Video Settings and restart.
helion.passive.incompatible_mod: Iris is installed. Helion stays inactive to avoid conflicts.
helion.sodium.title: Helion in Sodium mode
helion.sodium.message: Sodium draws the world, Helion adds its screen effects. Shadows, lighting and the sky are off.
helion.passive.render_failure: Helion hit an error and switched to vanilla rendering. See the log for details.
helion.parity.started: Comparing a vanilla frame with a Helion frame. Keep the camera still.
helion.parity.inactive: The parity check needs an active Helion render core.
helion.parity.busy: A parity check is already running.
helion.parity.aborted: Parity check stopped: the Helion frame could not be rendered because the render core was turned off or hit an error.
helion.parity.identical: Parity check passed: all %s pixels match vanilla.
helion.parity.different: Parity check: %s of %s pixels differ in color (largest channel difference %s), %s differ in depth (largest difference %s steps).
helion.parity.differences_image: Differing pixels are marked in screenshots/helion_parity_differences.png: red color only, yellow color and depth, blue depth only.
helion.parity.not_frozen: The game was not frozen, so clouds, particles and entities moved between the two frames. Run /tick freeze, keep the camera still and check again.
